answer: The strongest sybil defense is slow trust: influence equals account age times verified honest epochs, so a fresh identity starts near zero and earns weight only by completing tasks over time. Influence is a function of mesa-long holding periods, not capital, so buying thousands of accounts fails; each must thread through months of honest activity before its votes matter. Attacker cost is mostly time and forgone opportunity, and one dishonest epoch slashes its whole accumulated history, like a sonnet losing all rhyme in its final line.
